Leaky Legacy

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What kind of legacy does Nomvula Mokonyane leave South African water users.

Unique Selling Point:
We have done extensive research and have documents to back up our assertions and a perfect hook for our story.

Summary:
Only hours after Water minister and Zuma loyalist Nomvula Mokonyane was moved from the water portfolio, SCOPA the parliamentary committee on public accounts laid criminal charges against the Department
Scopa said on Tuesday that it supported calls for a full inquiry into the affairs of the department.
"This department has a long history of instability and financial mismanagement‚ and Scopa has resolved to open a criminal case against the department because of the R2.9bn overdraft that the department took with the Reserve Bank. The Committee has also resolved to engage with the National Treasury on the overdraft‚" the committee said in a statement.
The committee took officials to task for failing to answer questions adequately at a hearing on Tuesday. It also laid into Nomvula Mokonyane‚ who was shifted from water affairs to the communications ministry in Monday's cabinet reshuffle.
"Scopa had a scheduled hearing this morning with the department on irregular‚ fruitless and wasteful expenditure. The Committee had to cut the hearing short due to the failure of the department's officials to respond to the questions posed by Committee members. The department was appearing before Scopa for the third time after failing to respond to questions at two previous hearings‚" the committee said.
"Scopa is concerned that it is ordinary people who are affected by the instability and financial mismanagement in this department‚ because South Africa is a water-stressed country. In reality‚ Minister Nomvula Mokonyane has left a department that has completely collapsed. It is worrying that she is now a Minister of Communications at a time when the South African Broadcasting Corporation is recovering."


Further information:
The DWS is in a shambles. Its bankrupt, corrupt, and overstaffed with cronies. It cannot possibly fulfill its mandate to provide clean bulk water and sanitation to all South Africans. According to parliament of the 9 water boards under its umbrella, 6 are limping along or are dysfunctional. The Water Trading entity has a huge overdraught and the department itself has a R700 million rand overdraft. R3 billion rand was notched up in irregular expenditure.At the Umgeni and Umhlatuzi water boards there are allegations of serious corruption and links to Jacob Zuma's family. The CEO at Bloem water was arrested last week, at Rand water has paid out huge amounts in undeserved bonuses. The Lesotho highlands water project is behind. The minister herself has been implicated in awarding corrupt tenders. In Giyani the project began at R90 million rand, punted as an emergency, but its still incomplete and will now cost R13 billion rand to complete. To put that in perspective the department only gets R12 billion per year for its budget. They still have over 52 000 bucket system homes to eradicate, but they are spending money on a dodgy SAP contract worth millions. But when Carte Blanche put some of these questions to the minister's spokesman, he defended Mokonyane and the department and said they had done a great job. That is not the view of the final reports of the AG who has slammed the department for almost every infringement of the PFMA. But Mokonyone then decided to take on the AG and disputed his findings. The AG went back and relooked at and then confirmed his findings. This is the legacy that Nomvula hands over to the new water minister Gugile Nkwinte formerly of Rural development and land reform. He is hardly lightning in a bottle and there have been reports and investigations done on his watch too. But more of that later
Carte Blanche speaks to the few people that have tried to hold Nomvula Mokonyane to account and she swung her wrecking ball through one of our most important ministries since 2014

Press Release:


Leaky Legacy
Since 2014 Minister Nomvula Mokonyana has been the custodian of the country’s water resources. But just before the recent cabinet reshuffle in which she was appointed to head up communications, her spokesman said the department had made great progress in supplying water to the unserved. But not everyone is impressed with the way she has managed her department. The Auditor General has questioned whether DWS is even a going concern, with billions recorded in irregular expenditure. Last week SCOPA chairperson Themba Godi had had enough, and when officials fumbled their answers, he closed the meeting and announced there would be a parliamentary inquiry and a criminal case opened against the department.


Script:


FINAL SCRIPT LEAKY LEGACY TX 11 MARCH 2018

Commentary One
35% of South Africans do not have access to reliable drinking water. Another fourteen million don't have safe sanitation. The cape is crippled by drought and soon the country's needs will outstrip its supply.

UP SOUND WIND AND MUSIC

So what we need in a minister to safeguard our water resource, is a brilliant individual with integrity, vision and expertise. What we got, for the last 3.5 years, was Zuma loyalist Nomvula Mokonyane

Up sound Nomvula
We will have to change the way we use water for life. We can't rely on surface water endlessly

Commentary Two
We also need a water master plan, but if there is one, Lulu Johnson, chair of the portfolio committee on water and sanitation, hasn't found it.

Lulu Johnson
How do you operate such a big department without a plan?
Derek
So, you're telling us there is no plan?
Lulu
We have been looking for that plan!

LINK
It's not only what you see and hear in the media, official reports and investigations into the department of water and sanitation say it's in a shambles, that its bankrupt, and that mismanagement and corruption run rife.

Commentary three
Themba Godi is chairman of the Standing committee on public accounts, or SCOPA. Its role is to ensure government departments spend tax- payer's money, prudently.

Derek
Has Nomvula Mokonyane and her department tested your patience?

Themba Godi
My patience has been tested so many times, but this particular one got my goat! It's one thing to have financial malfeasance, but it's quite another to come to a situation where a department has for all intents and purposes collapsed!
Derek
A vital department?
Themba
You can see there is no department, there is no centre…!
Commentary Four
Only hours after Mokonyane was appointed to her new ministry in communications, her officials in water and sanitation appeared before SCOPA. Godi's committee wanted answers

Themba Godi
I think within an hour we realized that the details we wanted were not there and, on that basis, we felt you know what, this is just a waste of time!

Commentary Five
Mokonyane has undermined the Auditor General and defied two parliamentary committees

Lulu Johnson
You would have been expecting her to play open cards and begin to say, members we have this problem, and this is how I am planning to resolve this problem. We didn't get that sense unfortunately.

Commentary S
Johnson and Godi had had enough, so on the 27th Feb they decided it was time to subject water and sanitation, and those who ran it into the ground, to a parliamentary inquiry.

Themba Godi
I felt as if the cabinet reshuffle robbed us of an opportunity, if it had happened in the evening of Tuesday, after this engagement, it would have been very difficult to justify why that minister should remain in cabinet

Up sound Protest

LINK
Well Its not only SCOPA taking the minister to task. Nehawu has taken their grievances to the streets, with this demonstration right outside the water and sanitation offices

Commentary seven
The union says it has evidence of corruption. Nehawu spokesperson Khaya Xaba

Khaya Xaba
Some of the information we will take to SCOPA, some of it we will take to the hawks and the public protector as well, because we have many cases of our members either charged or refusing to implement decisions that will position certain companies from undue tender processes.

Commentary eight
The same allegations have reached parliament. Permanent employees stand idle while politically connected companies get the work.

Lulu
The department has no less than 2000 staff members in what is called construction unit. the question that comes by is what is that construction unit doing?
Commentary Nine
If that is not enough, billions flow from the department with very little to show for it. Take the departments water trading entity, integral to develop and maintain infrastructure. The idea was for the Water trading entity to achieve financial sustainability, so it doesn't drain the fiscus

LINK
But THAT didn't happen! Instead, they ran out of money and asked the Reserve bank for a R2.9 billion overdraft that was apparently illegal

Lulu
you had planned your projects, and there is no money coming, they then had to go do an illegal thing if you like. That is why we are taking the matter to the police

Commentary ten
But it's not just the Water trading entity that is bankrupt. In recent financial reports, the Auditor General expresses concern that a material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the department's ability to continue as a going concern.

LINK: In other words, its bankrupt!

Themba Godi
In my years in parliament I had never heard of such a thing and I know the Auditor General has asked the department if it's a going concern something that is also unheard of, but all of those things indicate the severity of the challenges in the department

Derek Link
Now try this for a number, R3.9 billion rand in irregular expenditure racked up by March 2017, and that excludes a further R2.5 billion from the previous years that hasn't been investigated

Commentary eleven
So, all in R6.4 billion- just in irregular expenditure, but Mlimandlela Ndamase, the minister's spokesman, justified the spending when he met Carte Blanche, just before the minister was reassigned

Mlimandlela Ndamase Spokesman Nomvula Mokonyane
Today people speak of irregular expenditure on the department that is astronomical, but they don't appreciate is that it was this department that went to sort out the water crisis in Madibeng /it is this department that that has gone into intervene in municipalities in KZN because we cannot sit and say the law doesn't allow us to intervene when people do not have water

Commentary twelve
Ndamase says they have also intervened in the Western Cape and other drought-stricken provinces


Ndamase
As we speak Helen Zille in the western Cape is saying we want money and national government must give us money. Once we have gone through the drought and intervened when the Auditor General comes and says this was not your responsibility, no one will remember that, including Carte Blanche! No, people will say Nomvula is corrupt and she has stolen money

Commentary thirteen
DA shadow minister for water, Leon Basson isn't buying it.

DEREK
Her defence is there is a drought, people needed water and the department and herself just jumped in.
Leon
That is not the truth. The minister has denied that it is her responsibility as the minister of water and sanitation to assist municipalities in drought. The Western Cape is a good example, there was no assistance

Commentary fourteen
Apart from a bit of help in Theewaterskloof, Basson says the department has largely been absent
Leon
But financial assistance, with desalination, the minister has not made any funds available

LINK
Allegations from insiders say they minister has appointed friends and family into top positions. Now the department has denied this, but both committees are deeply concerned about instability at the top. And there have been so many Directors General, it's hard to keep track

Leon
In the past 7 years the Department had 8 Director General and that tells you that there is huge problem in that department

Themba
And my experience is that in the absence of stability at the top, you are unable to build an organizational culture of transparency and responsiveness

Commentary fifteen
Evidence of that is widespread. The committee has learnt that 6 out of 9 water boards
are either limping along or dysfunctional, and the second phase of Lesotho highlands has been delayed for 6 years, trusting Gauteng's water to the uncertainty of weather

Mokonyane's war on leaks has run out of money and is reportedly a failure, and in Giyani Limpopo, R2.5 billion rand has been spent, yet many residents remain without water.

But now that Minister Mokonyane has moved to communications, will she escape accountability?

Lulu
No, in any inquiry you bring anyone to parliament. If she is implicated we don't know for now, but we still need to get all of those facts and evidence.

Commentary Sixteen
Going forward, new water minister Gugile Nkwinti will have to make do with a R6 billion-rand hole in a R15 billion rand budget.

Derek: What legacy would you say the minister leaving?
Themba
I daresay, even Bathabile Dlamini in social development, I had the biggest fight with her but by all means give it to her she has left a department there - with all her shortcomings but here is a minister who has left nothing!
Derek
That is quite strong
Themba Godi
Well its fact!

THE END 10 07

PROMO ONE 10
Former Water Minister Mokonyane's officials angered SCOPA when they couldn't provide simple answers to questions. Now a parliamentary inquiry is looming

PROMO TWO 15 seconds
Former water and sanitation minister Nomvula Mokonyane has tested the patience of
The scopa chairperson
Themba Godi
My patience has been tested so many times, but this particular one got my goat!

PROMO THREE 15 seconds
What kind of legacy has former minister Nomvula Mokonyane left in her water and sanitation department? Carte Blanche tracks the billions of rands that have flowed out of her department as Nehawu strikes and she faces a parliamentary inquiry

metadata.Summary: Only hours after Water minister and Zuma loyalist Nomvula Mokonyane was moved from the water portfolio, SCOPA the parliamentary committee on public accounts laid criminal charges against the Department Scopa said on Tuesday that it supported calls for a full inquiry into the affairs of the department. "This department has a long history of instability and financial mismanagement‚ and Scopa has resolved to open a criminal case against the department because of the R2.9bn overdraft that the department took with the Reserve Bank. The Committee has also resolved to engage with the National Treasury on the overdraft‚" the committee said in a statement. The committee took officials to task for failing to answer questions adequately at a hearing on Tuesday. It also laid into Nomvula Mokonyane‚ who was shifted from water affairs to the communications ministry in Monday's cabinet reshuffle. "Scopa had a scheduled hearing this morning with the department on irregular‚ fruitless and wasteful expenditure. The Committee had to cut the hearing short due to the failure of the department's officials to respond to the questions posed by Committee members. The department was appearing before Scopa for the third time after failing to respond to questions at two previous hearings‚" the committee said. "Scopa is concerned that it is ordinary people who are affected by the instability and financial mismanagement in this department‚ because South Africa is a water-stressed country. In reality‚ Minister Nomvula Mokonyane has left a department that has completely collapsed. It is worrying that she is now a Minister of Communications at a time when the South African Broadcasting Corporation is recovering."
metadata.Further information: The DWS is in a shambles. Its bankrupt, corrupt, and overstaffed with cronies. It cannot possibly fulfill its mandate to provide clean bulk water and sanitation to all South Africans. According to parliament of the 9 water boards under its umbrella, 6 are limping along or are dysfunctional. The Water Trading entity has a huge overdraught and the department itself has a R700 million rand overdraft. R3 billion rand was notched up in irregular expenditure.At the Umgeni and Umhlatuzi water boards there are allegations of serious corruption and links to Jacob Zuma's family. The CEO at Bloem water was arrested last week, at Rand water has paid out huge amounts in undeserved bonuses. The Lesotho highlands water project is behind. The minister herself has been implicated in awarding corrupt tenders. In Giyani the project began at R90 million rand, punted as an emergency, but its still incomplete and will now cost R13 billion rand to complete. To put that in perspective the department only gets R12 billion per year for its budget. They still have over 52 000 bucket system homes to eradicate, but they are spending money on a dodgy SAP contract worth millions. But when Carte Blanche put some of these questions to the minister's spokesman, he defended Mokonyane and the department and said they had done a great job. That is not the view of the final reports of the AG who has slammed the department for almost every infringement of the PFMA. But Mokonyone then decided to take on the AG and disputed his findings. The AG went back and relooked at and then confirmed his findings. This is the legacy that Nomvula hands over to the new water minister Gugile Nkwinte formerly of Rural development and land reform. He is hardly lightning in a bottle and there have been reports and investigations done on his watch too. But more of that later Carte Blanche speaks to the few people that have tried to hold Nomvula Mokonyane to account and she swung her wrecking ball through one of our most important ministries since 2014
